title: Unpaired Image-to-Image Translation using Cycle-Consistent Adversarial Networks
layout_note: Three panels (a), (b), (c) separated by dashed vertical rules: (a) the two mappings between the domains; (b) the forward cycle and its loss; (c) the backward cycle and its loss, mirroring (b).
grouping: Panels are separated by dashed vertical rules and labelled (a), (b), (c) below; (b) and (c) have the same structure.
shapes_depth: Plain black squares for the domains, curved arrows for the mappings, coloured dots for samples; serif math labels.
proposed_highlight: No highlight; each loss gets its own panel.
lesson: Give each loss its own panel of the same structure, so the reader compares the panels instead of untangling one diagram.
notes: year = arXiv preprint year; remembered venue ICCV 2017 (not verified in this session). Card written while studying arrangement (2026-11-15).

arrangement.units: three panels side by side behind dashed vertical rules; (b) and (c) are mirror images
arrangement.inputs_as: a domain square or sample at the left of each panel
arrangement.losses_at: each cycle-consistency loss inside its own panel, labelled with a dotted leader
arrangement.shared: the mappings G and F are redrawn in each panel

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

insights.structure: Three panels (a), (b), (c) separated by dashed vertical rules: (a) domains X and Y linked by mappings G and F with discriminators above; (b) forward cycle x -> Y_hat -> x_hat; (c) backward cycle mirroring (b).
insights.data: Domains are large squares with italic math letters; samples are blue and red dots inside domain squares; discriminators D_X, D_Y sit above with dotted up-arrows.
insights.emphasis: The cycle-consistency loss is a brace between the original and reconstructed dot with a dotted leader to the label, inside each cycle panel.
insights.flow: Left to right; curved arrows for mappings (G over the top, F underneath) and curved arcs between dots in the domain squares.
insights.avoid: Purely abstract: no example images, so the reader must already know what domains mean; monochrome styling gives no colour distinction between G and F.
